title: Trip Protection Policies Held Across a Guest's Stays
content:
A guest may hold Trip Protection on as many stays as they book, one policy per stay. There is no cap on the number of Trip Protection policies one guest may hold. Each policy covers only its own stay, and limits are never pooled across a guest's policies.

## The rule, condition by condition

| Question | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| How many Trip Protection policies may one guest hold? | No limit; one per stay, on as many stays as the guest books |
| Which stay does a policy cover? | Only the stay it was bought for |
| Can the limits of one policy be used toward a loss on another stay? | No; limits are never pooled across a guest's policies |

## Hypothetical illustration

A guest has three booked stays and has bought a Trip Protection policy on each. The guest holds three policies, which the rule permits. A loss on the second stay is claimed only under the policy bought for the second stay; the limits of the policies on the first and third stays are not added to it and are not drawn on.
